answer: An auditor observes that nectar credit accrues only on tasks whose reward curve is velvet-smooth: payouts rise linearly with milestones, fixed on chain before the task opens. A clone farm's signature is bursty income, so the auditor compares each payout series against the declared milestone schedule and flags any step a milestone curve cannot produce. Flagged accounts face tide-linked settlement: the payout window shifts one interval per flag, delaying withdrawals without confiscation. Honest agents feel nothing, since income follows the published curve.
